title: The work list
dek: What is being done here, as opposed to what is known.
lead: Every other register in this archive answers what is **known** — [what has been searched](/searched/), [what is still open](/open-questions/), [what was got wrong](/corrections/). None of them answered **what is being done**, so that lived in a chat window, which is the one place that does not survive the session. Three times in one week someone asked this archive what it was working on, and three times the answer was typed out and then lost. This is that answer, written down. It is deliberately short on findings and long on **who has to move each thing** — an item with no owner is how a list becomes wallpaper.
close:
Written 15 September 2026, in the shape the Defranceschi session settled on, so that eight archives keep one list rather than eight people each inventing one.

**Extended the same day into a roadmap.** The first twenty-two rows were what happened to be in hand. Rows 23 to 48 were built instead from what the archive already knows about itself: `coverage.json` says **34 of the 70 direct ancestors have no document**; `targets.json` ranks every filmed book by how many of them it would reach; `consistency.json` and `impossible.json` hold **116 contradictions** the tree has never been asked to explain. The rows are in yield order, and the yield is measured rather than guessed — **Karlobag deaths reach ten direct ancestors and that book's A–Z index is already mapped to the letter**, which is why it is row 23 and not row 40.

Three of them are not research at all but the conditions for it: **twenty-one ancestors have no place recorded**, so no film can be chosen for them (row 34); **a DGS number does not reliably name a book** (row 42); and **nobody has written down which parish the record index covers**, so every sitting rediscovers whether its next job is an hour or a week (row 43).

**And one gate added the same day, for the failure the list could not see in itself.** `checkworklist.py` checks the rows a list has; nothing checked the rows it was missing, and this list quietly showed **four letters where five had been sent**. `tools/checkcovers.py` now counts it against the register's **pending** rows and the contents of **`requests/sent/`**, and the build refuses when something outstanding has no row — or when a row still points at something retired. It caught **two more gaps** on its first run, and threw out its own first draft for containing an exemption that excused one of them.

rows.what: Rebuild the Žubrinić households of Šumećica by house number — all fifteen read
rows.note:
**All fifteen read, 15 September 2026, and [question 4](/open-questions/) 4d is answered: the Michaels are at least seven men, in seven houses, in four villages.** **Šumećica N° 5** (four children, 1849–58), **Šumećica N° 10**, **Poljica N° 13**, **Prozor N° 50**, **Obilje N° 7** and **Prozor Br. 1** — six distinct wives. The *Conditio* column separates them and nothing else does.

**Šumećica N° 5 is a household this archive did not have** — Michael Žubrinić and Maria Marković, four children across nine years. The Šumećica houses known before were N° 2, N° 10 and N° 24.

**Three Žubrinić women married Žubrinić men**, and the index carries a given name only for every one of them. **The index is also wrong at least once**: it gives the 1852 mother at Šumećica N° 5 as «Maria Maković» where the register says **Marković** — a household that looked like two is one.

The last entry, Maria of 28 November 1858, came in a third window: **Prozor N° 49**, next door to N° 50. Everything is in `sources/familysearch/otocac-michael-1846-1858.json`, and the cautions that cost this sitting time are in `notes/otocac-michael-house-numbers-2026-09-15.md` — the book **changes language from page to page**, the **status word drifts while the house number holds**, and entries hide in the last row of a left page below where a whole-page crop stops.

**Reconciled against the tree.** The households are not new people: all six wives and nine of the fourteen children are already there. **What the tree lacked was the house numbers** — of those nine children exactly one carried one, *Nikola Miko Žubrinić*, «Prozor 50», which this reading confirms; the rest said «Otočac, Croatia» or nothing. Seven are now in `sources/readings.psv`, and **five children genuinely absent from the tree** are in `sources/found.psv`, every one of them with siblings the tree already has.

**A caution worth more than the finding.** A first check concluded that none of the six wives was in the tree. That was wrong: they appear only as **parent references on their children**, with no page of their own, so a search of published people misses them. **Searching `people.json` is not searching the tree**, and a «not in the tree» claim made that way is worthless.

rows.what: Karlobag folios 6 and 4 — and ahnentafel 54's marriage, found on folio 4
rows.note:
**Found 15 September 2026, where this row expected a null.** Ahnentafel 54 married ahnentafel 55 at Karlobag on **17 June 1807**, folio 4, image 231: «…habito mutuo consensu ***Georgii filij defti Georgii Uroda*** et ***Mariæ filiæ Michaelis Gergas*** hujatium… præsentibus testibus *Caspare Jerko viduo* et *Joanne Fero…*». The date column reads 17 and the month is a ditto for the entry above it, *16 Junii*; the page runs 7 Jan · 14, 22, 26 *ejusdem* · 3 Feb · 7 May · 16 Jun · **17** · 8 Jul · 20 Sep, so the ditto can only be June.

**It proves the two brothers.** The 1806 marriage of *Joannis filii defuncti Dñi Georgij Uroda* was read at the time as probably a brother rather than ahnentafel 54 himself, because ahnentafel 55's 1834 death entry calls her husband a *Georgius*. Confirmed from the other side: **Joannes and Georgius are both sons of the same dead Georgius Uroda**, married sixteen months apart in the same church. Ahnentafel 108 is named here as «defti Georgii Uroda», tying the 1791 burial to both marriages.

**Two cautions.** The volume's own index put a Georgius Uroda on **folio 6** — folio 6 has now been read **end to end, both pages, 1809 and 1810 through to the «Finis», and holds no Uroda at all**. The index's *folium* column does not reliably name the leaf. And the doubt carried as «Martini U[roda?]» in the 18 January 1809 entry reads, at five times full resolution, **Uzelac** — settled, and not a lead. Full record in `notes/karlobag-1807-uroda-gergas.md`.

rows.what: Selce deaths — ahnentafel 24 and 25 read, and the cholera that took him
rows.note:
**Ahnentafel 25 is read, 15 September 2026.** LIBER DEFUNCTORUM p. 144, image 397: «**Udova Maria Antić, supruga pok. Josipa, kći Jurja i Mare Jeličić, R. Katolikinja**» — Selce house **29**, aged **73**, died **6 July 1882**, buried the 7th. Widow of ahnentafel 24, daughter of ahnentafel 50, and the age matches a birth of 22 March 1809. The mother is written «Mare» where the tree has ahnentafel 51 as *Margarita* — consistent, not proof, recorded as read.

**The index does not cover this register, which changes how the rest gets done.** A sweep for *Antić* at Selce returns **119 indexed entries and every one is a baptism**. The index-with-ARK shortcut that found the Otočac households and the Karlobag baptism in minutes **does not work here** — this book has to be walked.

**So the film is mapped instead.** 005497948 is 802 images and is not one book: image 200 is a *HISTORIA PAROCHIAE*, the death register runs through the 380s–390s, image 600 is a later Croatian-ruled register, and **the waypoint in the URL changes between images**. Measured: **384 = 1877**, **397 = 1882**, **400 = 1883–84** — about **2.7 images to the year**.

**Ahnentafel 24 is read, 15 September 2026.** Page 99, image 340, ARK `3:1:3QSQ-G99X-13PY`: «*Letta 850. **na 21. 8bre*** · house **74** · **Preminu Osip Antić težak i Mare kćer** · **44 / 6** · ***Od kolere***». **One entry for two people** — Josip and his six-year-old daughter Mare, dead the same day of **cholera**. The age puts his birth in 1805–06 and the tree says 14 March 1806. His house is **74**, not the **29** where his widow died in 1882 — two numbers, thirty-two years and a widowhood apart, recorded as two.

**The page is a casualty list.** *Od kolere* runs down the remarks column; pages 98–99 hold 30 September to 21 October 1850, six deaths on the 10th alone, and **seven other Antić deaths in the eleven days before Josip**. None is claimed.

**A false null was nearly written and the page numbers stopped it** — 99, [100], 101 across images 340 and 341, so the jump from 21 October 1850 to 21 February 1851 is a real gap in the dying, not a lost leaf. Written up in [notes/selce-cholera-1850.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/selce-cholera-1850.md).

**The year map was wrong and is fixed.** Not 2.7 images to the year: **311 = 1834**, **338 = early 1849**, **339–340 = Sept–Oct 1850**, **341 = 1851–52** — about **1.7** through the 1830s–50s, 2.7 only in the 1870s–80s. Arks in `sources/familysearch/film-005497948-selce-deaths.json`.

**What is left is [row 25](/worklist/):** ahnentafel 48 and 49 (1829, ≈ image 302) and 96, 98 and 99 in the 1790s–1800s.

rows.what: Ahnentafel 53's baptism — found: Oliva Maria Smojver, 11 March 1781
rows.note:
**Found 15 September 2026.** «Ego Joës Antonius Frankovich Parochus Loci baptizavi Infantem ***die 11ma*** hujus natam ex ***Vincentio, et Oliva Smoyver, vulgò Vukić***, Conjugibus hujus Civitatis, cui imposui est nomen ***Oliva Maria***» — Karlobag, page 65, ark `3:1:3QS7-L99C-L998-5`. The month column reads *Ejusdem* under *Martij*, and the next opening begins at 19 March, so **11 March 1781**. The tree had only «MAR 1781».

**It confirms ahnentafel 106 and 107 from the register side** — Vicentius Smojver Vukić and Oliva Bacchi were in the tree but had never been put on a page; one line now names the couple and the child together.

**And it gives a by-name in a parish that had none.** «Smoyver, ***vulgò*** Vukić» — this archive's by-name file was built out of Selce, where the connectors are *aliter · dictus · dicti* and the scribe **underlines** the pair. Karlobag uses ***vulgò*** and does **not** underline. It also explains a name the tree carries without comment: ahnentafel 106 is recorded as «Vicentius Fabiano Smojver **Vukić**» as though Vukić were part of the surname. It is the household name, and the clerk said so.

**A film note this corrects.** `holdings.psv` gives DGS 5481648 as the 1691–1804 baptisms and `notes/karlobag-films.md` calls it a **327-image** film with «image 220 = Anno Domini 1782». Film 005481648 actually has **596 images** and its image 216 is headed **«Godine 1845»**. The 1771–1804 baptisms are under a different waypoint, and the way in was the **record index**, not the film number. Full record in `notes/karlobag-1781-oliva-smojver.md`.

rows.what: Reconcile the stale «pending» rows in the searched register
rows.note:
**Done 15 September 2026.** Three rows were retired, not edited: **Ancestry**, **FamilySearch — Rijeka registers** and **FamilySearch — Otočac, Stanje duša** were *placeholders* — «never», «not yet», «still unread» — and each had been superseded by a real row recording the actual reading. The register was **over-reporting what is outstanding**: eleven pending, of which three were already done. Seven now, and every one of them genuinely open.

**The gate that stops it recurring.** Every register row now declares a `key` — the body of material it covers — and `tools/searched.py` **refuses** when a row is *pending* while any other row with the same key carries a real outcome. The key is there because the source *name* cannot do this job: «Senj marriages, 1734–1858» is genuinely unopened while «Senj marriages, 1859–1920» is read end to end, and a gate matching on names would have called the first one stale and sent a sitting to re-read a book that was already finished. A gate that cries wolf is worse than no gate.

The same stale claim had spread into prose: `/searched` still named **four portals «never once searched»** when all four had been opened, and `requests/README.md` and `REPLIES.md` still said the three letters were **not yet sent** when they went on the 15th. All corrected.

rows.what: Decide where ahnentafel 108 and 109 live
rows.note: **Georgius Uroda** and his wife **Maria** were read out of a register this week and are real. rows.what: Državni arhiv u Rijeci — answered, and it is a refusal
rows.note:
**Answered 15 September 2026, the same day it was sent.** Boris Zakošek: «**Državni arhiv u Rijeci ne provodi ovako složena rodoslovna istraživanja.** Istraživati možete sami u čitaonici Arhiva ili putem internetske stranice familysearch.org» — *the archive does not carry out genealogical research of this complexity; research it yourself in the reading room or on FamilySearch.*

**It refuses the service without answering about the holdings.** The letter asked one question needing no research: whether they **hold, or know who holds, the Rijeka baptismal register covering 1 March 1892**. That is unanswered, and it matters — the 1892–99 volume is missing from the film and from its Kazalo both, which is why Ljubomir Blažević's baptism has never been placed.

**The reply points back at FamilySearch**, which the letter had already said — quoting the volume list — has been read to the end with a gap exactly there.

**What is left is the reading room**, which is genuinely offered: this is material that can be consulted in person at Rijeka, by David or by a paid local researcher. That is now the only stated route to the 1892 entry, and it is a decision rather than a task.

rows.note:
**Answered 15 September 2026, the same day, by vlč. Jakov Filipović, župnik.** «**Matice i arhiva svih župa kojim upravljam je predata u Riječku Nadbiskupiju.** Koliko mi je poznato **oni su istu predali na skrb Državnoga Arhiva.** Budući mi ovdje na župama **nemamo dodir sa starijim Maticama**, za daljnje informacije kontaktirajte **Ured riječke nadbiskupije**.»

**It corrects the assumption this whole line of letters rested on.** The reason for writing to parish offices was the Senj archive's instruction plus a belief that *the books the films do not cover are the ones that never left parish custody*. **For Krmpote that is simply wrong.** The registers went to the Archdiocese, and the priest has no contact with his own older books.

**Nothing was refused.** Juraj Blažević's baptism, his marriage, his death and the Butorac marriage are all still wanted; they are just not in this man's hands, and he said so kindly and at once.

**The door it opens is [row 52](/worklist/).**

rows.note: Fifteen nodes named with a single capital letter — **«M Žubrinić Xubrinich Zubrinic»** — were being published as parents of 75 real people and as one another's siblings. A card index typed in as a family. Both the bucket detector and the site's junk filter now refuse them, **but all seven archives share one GEDCOM**, and nothing here has checked whether the same drawers exist under Blažević, Papić, Prpić or Kalanj. **The test is four lines** and belongs in the kit rather than in this archive.

rows.what: Six methods found here that the other archives will need
rows.note:
**The index gives the image.** FamilySearch's record search returns the **image ARK** of every indexed entry, so a record opens at the page in one step instead of being hunted down a film — that single fact produced most of this week's findings. **A third FamilySearch failure state**: a sign-out takes *everything* (503, redirect to the sign-in host) where a rate-limit blip and a session block leave the catalogue answering — written into `tools/familysearch.md`. **And `sources/found.psv`**, somewhere to put people read out of a register whom the tree does not have; every archive here will hit that wall.

**Fourth — the register cannot be trusted to retire its own rows.** `/searched` here said eleven sources were outstanding when three had been read and closed: each was a «not yet» placeholder left standing because the reading went into a *new* row. Over-reporting what is outstanding is the same lie as under-reporting it, and it costs a sitting that re-opens a finished book. The fix generalises: **every row declares a `key` naming the body of material it covers, and the checker refuses a *pending* row when another row with that key has a real outcome.** The key is the whole trick — matching on the source *name* would flag «Senj marriages, 1734–1858», which is genuinely unopened, against «Senj marriages, 1859–1920», which is read end to end. Every archive that keeps a search register has this bug waiting in it. In `tools/searched.py` here.

**Fifth — there is a fourth FamilySearch failure state, and it is the worst one.** Beside the rate-limit blip, the session block and the sign-out, there is **Error 15**: a 403 «Access Denied» interstitial on *every* path, laid on the egress address rather than the session. Signing in again does nothing. **The diagnostic that tells it apart in one call** is to fetch a Deep Zoom `image.xml` for an ark that read successfully before: a blip or a session block leaves the tile edge answering, and Error 15 takes the tiles down too. If the tiles are gone there is no route to a page and the only moves are to wait or to read from a different network.

**Sixth — a work list cannot see its own omissions, and needs a second list to count against.** The kit's `checkworklist.py` gates the rows a list *has*. Nothing gated the rows it was *missing*, and on 15 September this archive had **five letters sent and four rows** — the missing one being the reply that named three further doors, and therefore the reason three of the other rows existed. **Every row present looked fine in isolation. The list was only wrong in what it did not say.**

`tools/checkcovers.py` here counts the work list against two lists that are already exact: every **`pending` row in the search register** (which means, in the register's own words, «known, wanted, and not yet got») and every letter in **`requests/sent/`**. A row declares what it accounts for in a `covers` field, and the build refuses when something outstanding has no row — **or when a row points at something that no longer exists**, which is how a list goes stale rather than short.

**It found two real gaps on its first run** — Brinje, pending since the 14th with no row, and ahnentafel 11 — and it **rejected its own first draft**: that draft exempted keys beginning `plan/` as «not really work», and the one row so excused turned out to name two baptisms sitting in a book already open. The exemption was noise-reduction dressed as a rule, and there is none now.

**Every archive in the estate keeps a work list and a search register**, so every one of them can be short in exactly this way, and none of them can currently tell.

Every `git add` here stays scoped to `sources/ tools/ site/src/ notes/ requests/`.

rows.what: Harvest house numbers from the Otočac baptisms of 1834–46
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake, and it was this archive's own.** The morning's plan said *every* entry writes the household into the *Conditio* column. **That book does not**: its *Conditio* holds one status word — *Confiniarius*, *Decurio* — checked at December 1839 and March 1845, with the place column giving only «Ottoccii». Ahnentafel 10's January 1834 entry is an early-book habit the parish dropped. **House numbers are readable for 1846–58 and for the first years of 1834, and not in between.**

rows.what: Working when the route out is narrow — FamilySearch's block, and the hidden pane
rows.note:
**Error 15, and it comes and goes.** On 15 September 2026 every request to `familysearch.org` began returning **403 «Access Denied — Error 15»** as a full interstitial. It shut at 04:21, opened at 04:30, shut at 04:45, opened at 04:47, shut at 04:51 and opened again at 05:00. **Fifteen register entries were read in those windows**, which is the whole of work list row 1.

**So the lesson is not «wait for it to clear».** It is to have the targets — ARKs, dates, parents — written to disk *before* a window opens, so a ten-minute opening is ten minutes of reading rather than ten minutes of searching. That is what `sources/familysearch/otocac-michael-1846-1858.json` is, and it is why row 1 closed on a day when the site was mostly shut.

**The one-call diagnostic.** Fetch a Deep Zoom `image.xml` for an ARK that read successfully before: a rate-limit blip or a session block leaves the tile edge answering, and Error 15 takes the tiles down too. If `image.xml` returns HTML instead of `<?xml`, there is no route to a page — not the index, not the catalogue, not the scans. Signing in again does nothing; the block is on the egress address, not the session.

**Client IP 168.140.255.212.** Reading from David's own browser on his own network would not be behind this address at all.

---

**A second constraint, and it is the binding one. 15 September 2026: the Browser pane is hidden in the app, and a hidden pane cannot take a screenshot.** Every read of a register scan in this archive goes through one — crop, enlarge, look. Without it, three routes were tried and all three failed:

* **Post the image to a local server.** The page cannot reach `127.0.0.1` at all: the in-app browser applies the private-network rule and an `https` page on familysearch.org gets «Failed to fetch», with no CSP report, for both `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`.
* **Fetch the Deep Zoom tiles from the shell.** `image.dzi` answers **403** with a bot interstitial and the tile path answers **401**. The tiles want the session, and the session is not something this archive will copy out of a browser.
* **Carry the image out as base64 through a tool result.** This *works at small sizes* — a whole page at contact-sheet scale is about 3 KB and arrived intact. It **fails at useful sizes**. A 19,891-byte contact sheet came back with **exactly the right byte count and the wrong SHA-256**: characters substituted, not dropped, silently. Chunking to 76-character lines did not help.

**So there is a ceiling of a few kilobytes, and a register entry at full resolution is above it.** That matters more than it sounds: this archive's own standing rule is that **no date, name or house number is recorded from a page-scale view**, and it exists because a *19* reads as *1* and a flat-topped *2* reads as *7*. Reading through a channel that can alter bytes without saying so would break that rule in a way nothing downstream could catch.

**Text is not affected and was used hard.** The catalogue is JSON, so [row 42](/worklist/)'s eighty-six film notes came out whole and were **verified by SHA-256 against a second fetch** before being written down. That is the shape of the workaround: **anything that can be checksummed can come out; a photograph cannot.**

**Showing the Browser pane again puts rows 4, 6, 7, 24–35 and 54 back within reach.**

rows.what: The people found beside the tree are published — and the list got shorter

rows.what: Karlobag deaths 1774–1804 — all four ancestors read, and a widow the index hides
rows.note:
**Corrected 15 September 2026 before it was begun: this is a walk, not a lookup.** The row was written asserting the Karlobag deaths could be reached through the FamilySearch index. They cannot — row 43 tested four surnames and **every Karlobag hit is a baptism**; the 1717–1861 range that suggested otherwise is baptisms throughout.

**The highest-yield target in the archive, and it is already mapped.** `targets.json` says the Karlobag death books reach **ten direct ancestors** — ahnentafel 52, 55, 104, 105, 107, 108, 110, 111, 212 and 220 — more than any other book here. Four of them have **exact death dates inside the 1774–1804 volume**: ahn 212 Josiph Smojver Vukić **16 May 1776**, ahn 104 Jacob Pilipić **10 April 1778**, ahn 220 Nicolaus Gerkacs **30 October 1783**, ahn 105 Catherina Luckinić **29 May 1790**. Ahn 108's burial of 10 September 1791 is already read out of this same book.

**And it needs no walking.** `holdings.psv` records the register at images **356–409** and its **KAZALO A–Z at 410–434, with the letter positions measured** — P.R at 428, R.S 429, S.T 430, T.U 431, U.V 432, V.X 433. Look up *Pilipić*, *Smojver*, *Gerkacs* and *Luckinić* in the index, take the folium, convert with the known folio map (left pages EVEN, folio 62 = image 388), and read four ancestors in an afternoon.

**What the index page actually looks like, now it has been opened.** Image 428 is **P on the left page and R on the right** — the big letter is written at the top centre of each *page*, three column-groups to a page, each *Cognomen · Nomen · dies · folium*. **The entries are ordered by folio, not alphabetically within the letter**: folios 104, 104, 105, 105, 105, 106, 106, reading Perpich · Perpich · Perpich · Perpich · Potocgniak · **Pekkas** · Potocgniak. So a surname is found by scanning the letter's pages, not by jumping to it. Folio converts to image as **image = 388 + (folio − 62) ÷ 2**, left pages even.

**A find already, from the one index page opened:** *«Pekkas Magdalena, 5 Augusti, folio 106»*. **Pekass is three of the direct ancestors with no document** — ahn 213, 426 and 427 — and this is the first time the surname has appeared in a register here at all.

---

**Begun and half done, 15 September 2026. The KAZALO works.**

**Ahnentafel 104 is read** — folio **17**, image **364**, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-GSBG`:

> «**10: Aprilis** · **D. Jacobus Pilepich Capitaneus portûs**, munitus omnibus Sacramentis per M.R. D. Andream Pintor Capellanum Loci, **spiritum Deo reddidit**, … **in propria Crypta in Parochiali Ecclesia existente**, per me Joannem … tumulatus est»

**Three marks of standing in one entry, and this archive had none of them.** ***Capitaneus portûs*** — **captain of the port**, a crown office in a Military Frontier harbour. The ***D.*** is *Dominus*, withheld from the *Decurio* and the *infans* on the same opening. And he is **not in the parish cemetery**: he is in **his own crypt inside the church**. No age is given. [The note](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/karlobag-1778-jacobus-pilepich.md).

**The route, for the three still to do.** Image **427**, right page, is the letter **P** — three dense columns, ordered **by folio**, not alphabetically. «*Pillepich Jacobus · 10 Aprilis · **folio 17***» sits in the third. Then **folio → image**, measured directly: image 364 = folios **16|17**, image 365 = **18|19**, so `image = 356 + folio ÷ 2`. **That disagrees with `holdings.psv` by one** — it puts folio 62 at **387** where the file says **388**. **Read the folio number printed at the top of the page**, every time.

**Ahnentafel 212 is read too — folio 11, image 361, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-G3WG`:** «*16 ejusdem [Maij 1776] · **Josephus Smojver dictus Vukcich, annorum 45**, munitus omnibus [Sacramentis] … in Domino obijt, atque die 17 … in Coemeterio Parochiali tumulatus*». **The tree's date to the day**, and *annorum 45* agrees with its 1731.

**He is not under S. He is under V** — «***Vukich — vide Smojver — 16: Maij — folio 11***». **This KAZALO indexes the household by-name as a headword** and cross-references it to the surname, and does the same on the same page for «*Verbanovich … **vide Urbanovich***». **A surname missing from its own letter is not absent from the book.** For a family already known here as «*Smoyver **vulgò** Vukić*» (1781), that is the difference between an ancestor and a null — and the 1776 entry uses a different connector, ***dictus***.

**Ahnentafel 220 is read** — folio **39**, the right-hand page of image **376**, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-GSBH`: «*30 8bris · **Nicolaus Gergacs annorum 66**, munitus omnibus sacramentis obiit … **in domo filij sui Antonij**, et **die 31: ejusdem** … sepultus est in Cœmeterio … Laterali ex parte dextra Ecclesiæ Parochialis hujus*». **The tree's date to the day**, *annorum 66* agreeing with its 1717 — and **he died in his son Antonius's house**, a Gergacs this archive has never published.

**Two things the sitting taught.**

* **The KAZALO's date can be the burial.** It says «*3i 8bris*»; the register says died the **30th**, buried «*die 31: ejusdem*». That is exactly what [Find a Grave](/port-pirie/) does — a cemetery records the interment, a parish the death — and **a parish index does it too**. Use the index date to *find* an entry, never to record one.
* **The folio arithmetic drifts; the index does not.** Interpolating from folio 17 put folio 39 on image 375, one leaf early, on a page that ends at 18 June 1783. The printed number settled it in one crop. **Interpolate, then read the number at the top of the page.**

**Letter positions measured: G** 418 right (419 left is G and empty), **P** 427–428, **R** 428, **S** 429, **T** 430, **V** 432.

**Ahnentafel 105 is read, and she closes the row** — folio **63**, image **388**, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-G3QY`: «*29 ejusdem [Maij 1790] · **Catharina annorum 70, vidua defti Jacobi [P]ilepich**, obiit in Domino munita omnibus sacramentis, atque **die 30** sepulta est*». **The tree's date to the day** — and what identifies her is her husband's name, not her own: she is the widow of **ahnentafel 104**, the port captain, dead twelve years before her. **The age disagrees**: 70 in May 1790 puts her birth about **1720** where the tree says **30 March 1727**. Recorded, not resolved.

**She is not in the KAZALO's L, and the whole of L was read to prove it** — folios **1–73** and **76–102**, group 3 blank, image 423's L page empty. Five Luckinić entries, none Catharina. **A widow is indexed under her husband's surname**, which is the third time today this archive has met that rule: «*Vukich vide Smojver*», the Senj stones carving a married woman under her husband's name, and now the KAZALO. Two more by-name headwords fell out of the search — «*Ljubicich **dictus** Luxich ut ibi*» and «*Locatelli, **vulgò** Zessich*».

**Year map for this volume**, measured: folio 17 = 1778 · 39 = 1783 · **63 = 1790** · 74 = 1793 — about **3.5 folios to the year**. From image 376 to 394 it is exactly two folios per image; between 364 and 376 it is not.

**All four ancestors in this book are read.** The next one is [row 24](/worklist/), the *Umrli 1804–1861* on the same film, whose own alphabetical index a previous sitting already found at images ~168–192.

**And the index has put Pekass on the table.** Five entries — *Pekas Anton* folio 1, *Blasius* folio 2, *Maria* folio 5, *Joanna* folio 10, *Pekkas Magdalena* folio 106. **Pekass is ahnentafel 213, 426 and 427**, three direct ancestors with no document at all, and the surname had never appeared in a Karlobag register here. **These are index lines, not readings** — no page has been opened.

rows.what: Selce deaths — ahnentafel 48 and 49 read; three ancestors left in the 1790s and 1800s
rows.note:
Row 3 read **ahnentafel 25** (1882) and **ahnentafel 24** (1850, of cholera). **Ahnentafel 48 and 49 are now read too**, both on image **304**, ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99X-1QQL`:

> «*Die **13ᵃ Martii 1829*** · house **51** · ***Joannes Antich Papa**. obiit Annorum **64***»
>
> «*Die **15ᵉ Julii 1829*** · house **56** · ***Margarita uxor Joannis Antich <u>Natanchii</u> obiit Annorum 52***»

**Both dates are the tree's to the day and both ages fit its birth years**, 1765 and 1777. **The houses differ and so do the by-names** — his *Papa*, hers *Natanchii* and **underlined**. One household with two names, a widow moved to a child's house, or two different couples: [the note](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/selce-antic-1829-papa.md) takes none of the three. The marriage, or the Selce *Status Animarum*, would settle it.

**And «Papa» is [question 5](/open-questions/)'s word** — here fifty-six years before the Senj «*Juraj Papa*» and behind a different surname. Not a link between the families: **evidence that *Papa* was a by-name in circulation**, and therefore weak evidence of descent wherever it stands alone.

**Three direct ancestors are left in this book**: ahn **96** (Joannis Antić, 27 Feb 1793), **98** (Pauli Lončarić, 29 Sep 1811) and **99** (Anna Papić, 24 Aug 1807). `targets.json` scores the book **19 reachable of 19** — the only one in the archive where every reachable person is a direct ancestor or their sibling.

**The year map is measured now, and it runs back as well as forward**: 302 = 1828, 304 = 1829, 311 = 1834, 338 = early 1849, 339–340 = Sept–Oct 1850, 341 = 1851–52, 384 = 1877, 397 = 1882 — about **1.7 images to the year** here. **1811 lands near image 273, 1807 near 266, 1793 near 242**, all far outside the measured range, and the film changes books more than once.

**And read the printed page number before writing any negative** — it is in the top outer corner of the right-hand leaf.

rows.what: Otočac deaths — ahnentafel 40 and 41 both read, and a false null corrected
rows.note:
**The best direct-line target at Otočac, now that row 27 is corrected.** Two ancestors are unread and **both have exact death dates inside the filmed 1834–1858 book**:

* **Ahnentafel 40, Toma Žubrinić**, died **4 January 1838** — and the tree places him at ***Šumećica 2***.
* **Ahnentafel 41, Marija Findrić**, died **29 July 1849**.

**Ahn 40 is the one that matters beyond himself.** Šumećica N° 2 is the house where row 1 found Nicolaus Žubrinić baptising children in 1856 and 1858. **A death entry naming that house would tie the direct line to a house number that is currently only inferred** — which is the whole of question 4.

**It is a walk, not a lookup.** Otočac is indexed for **baptisms only** — 165 in the sample and not one death — so the index cannot be used here ([row 43](/worklist/)). The deaths sit on **DGS 5482657**, the same film as the 1846–58 baptisms already read for row 1, so the film is known ground even though the section is not.

**Unblocked and opened, 15 September 2026 — after a sitting lost to the film number.** `…/search/film/005482657?i=N` reports 483 images; **the Otočac book is 218**, and past that the traversal crosses into **Pakrac**, which is why four sampled images were all baptisms and a first conclusion said the deaths were not filmed. They are. Waypoint `9RK1-Y4C:391644801,391674001`; image **100** is 1835, **165** is 1849, **200** is 1855. ARKs in `sources/familysearch/otocac-deaths-1834-1858.json`.

**It is the right instrument.** The far-right column is the running entry number — it restarts at **1** under each ruled year heading — and the entry text carries the village and house — «*Confiniarii e Prozor N° 40*». Exactly what question 4 needs.

**Ahnentafel 41 is read too — image 167, page 153, entry 53.** «*Leta 1849 dne **29 Srpnja** preminula je · **Maria Žubrinić, Udovica** · **69** · Slaboća starosti po dokazu Lečnika · u župničkoj grobnici*». ARK `3:1:3QS7-899C-PVHR`. **The date to the day, the age against the tree's 1780, and the widowhood all agree** — Toma died eleven years earlier. **But no house and no husband are named**, so her entry is not anchored to Šumećica N° 2 the way his is, and this row does not pretend it is.

**And a correction, recorded because it is the useful part.** An earlier pass today read page 151 as ending *28 Srpnja* and page 152 as opening *9 Kolovoza*, and concluded **no death was recorded on 29 July 1849 at all**. Every month in that sentence was wrong: 151 runs **4 *Svibnja* (May) to 8 *Lipnja* (June)**, 152 runs **9 *Lipnja* to 14 *Srpnja* (July)**, and the «*Kate, žena Mate Žubrinića*» entry is **7 May**. July had not been reached. The entry numbers did run continuously — which is what made the wrong conclusion feel safe. **A continuous sequence proves no page is missing; it proves nothing about which months are on it.** Written up in [notes/otocac-marija-findric-1849.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/otocac-marija-findric-1849.md).

**Ahnentafel 40 is read — image 117, page 45, entry 3 of 1838.** «*1838. Januarii die 4ta · **Thomas Xubrinich**, Inq: ~~Ottoèsanq~~ Centu-rio **Confiniarius, ex Pago Shumcchicza N° 2** · **An. 70** · Senectutis Debilitas*». ARK `3:1:3QS7-L99C-PVR4`. **The tree's date, the tree's house and the tree's birth year are all corroborated at once**, for a man who had no media at all. He does not move into house 2 from anywhere — he dies in it, eighteen years before his grandson's children are baptised out of it, and **the «he moved / it is another Nicolaus» pair is no longer level**. Written up in [notes/otocac-toma-zubrinic-1838.md](https://github.com/daviddef/TheBlazevic/blob/main/notes/otocac-toma-zubrinic-1838.md).

**And the book turns out to be worth more than two ancestors.** The Otočac *baptisms* stop writing the household into *Conditio* from about **1836 to 1845**; **the deaths write the village and house straight through those years**. This book is the house-number source for the window the baptisms cannot reach.

rows.what: Senj deaths — all three ancestors read, and the age column exposed
rows.note:
**All three read, 15 September 2026.** Ahnentafel **27** (9 Feb 1886), **8** (26 Jul 1907) and **26** (14 Nov 1897) are each at the page, and every date matches the tree to the day.

**What they add.** Ahn 26 is *«finan.… u miru»* — a **retired finance man**; ahn 8 is a ***nadničar***, a day labourer. Neither had an occupation here before, and the two Senj households sit either side of a line. **Karlobag** is recorded as the origin of *both* ahn 26 and ahn 27, confirming the birthplaces the tree carries and putting the whole couple in Karlobag before Senj. And ahn 8's entry touches **ahnentafel 9** for the first time — *«Udovac iza pok. Tereze»*.

**The finding worth more than the entries: the age column is hearsay, and the clerk says so.** Ahn 26's age is written ***«navodno 93 god.»*** — *reportedly* 93 — against a true 91. Ahn 27's reads 78 against 75. Ahn 8's reads 69 and is exactly right. **An age in this book is what the informant said**, never a document, and it must never be used to date a birth where a baptism exists.

**Two indexing traps recorded.** Ahn 27 is filed under **Pilipić**, her married name — a search for *Uroda* finds nothing. Ahn 26 is filed under **Pilepić**, a different spelling from his own wife's entry in the same office eleven years earlier.

rows.what: Twenty-one ancestors with no place — and two of them had one all along
rows.note:
Of the **34 direct ancestors without a document**, **21 have no place recorded — not a village, not a parish, in several cases not a date either**: ahn 22, 41, 64, 80, 84, 85, 86, 87, 97, 100, 101, 102, 103, 109, 128, 210, 211, 213, 427, 428, 429. **No amount of film-reading reaches them**, because nothing says which film to open. This row is the precondition for half the rows above it.

The method that works is the one that found ahnentafel 55's father: **a person with no record of their own is named in their child's**. Every one of these twenty-one has a child in the tree; the child's baptism or marriage entry names the parent and usually the village. So the job is to **work down from the children**, not up from the parents.

---

**Two came off the list on 15 September without any film being opened, because they were never placeless.**

The list was built from the wall grading, and the wall grading called a household **«No place recorded»** whenever no parish in `parishes.psv` claimed its village. That is not the same thing. The tree gives **ahnentafel 426** as born at **Smiljan, Općina Gospić** and **ahnentafel 222** at **Montani Stanište** — both written plainly, both printed for weeks under «*No place is recorded for this household anywhere on the line*».

**`walls.py` now separates the two**, with a new grade **`ungazetteered`** — *«The tree does record where this household was … but no parish in this archive's table claims that village … This is not a wall in the record. It is a gap in the gazetteer.»* **Nineteen of the twenty-one are genuinely placeless. Two are one line of `parishes.psv` away**, and that line is [row 56](/worklist/).

**A third came off earlier the same day**: ahnentafel **220**, placed at Karlobag by his own death entry. So the twenty-one is **eighteen**, and the method the row proposed — *work down from the children* — has not been started yet.

---

**Three more came off the list on 15 September, and again no film was opened.** The wall grading looked at **one field on two people** — the person's own `bornPlace`, then the ahnentafel child's — and called everything else *«No place is recorded for this household anywhere on the line»*. That sentence was false three more times.

* **Ahnentafel 102, Joanni Brozović** — his daughter Margarita is recorded as **dying at Selce**. A death place is a place.
* **Ahnentafel 103, Catharina**, his wife — the same daughter, the same parish.
* **Ahnentafel 427, Mara Pekass** — her husband is recorded as **born at Smiljan**, and the grading never once looked at a spouse, though it had been computing one all along. **A husband's parish is his wife's.**

**The fallback now runs through the household, nearest first** — own death, child's birth, child's death, spouse's birth, spouse's death — and **each wall says which relation supplied it**: *«This household is put at Selce on the strength of their child's death — the tree's own words about the tree's own people, not a document.»* That distinction is the whole point. Nothing here was read off a page, and a wall that pretended otherwise would be worse than one that said nothing.

**Four are genuinely placeless and always were**: **ahnentafel 84 and 86, Vitus and Michael Sekula**; **128, Mateša Blažević**; **428, Angelo Bacchi**. Not a village, not a death place, not a spouse, not a child with either. For these four the row's original method — work down from the children's baptisms — is still the only way in, and it still needs a register.

rows.what: Gologorica — twenty-four Šestani, and not one direct ancestor
rows.note:
`parishes.psv` carries **Gologorica** with *unknown* in all three range columns and the note «Istria — likely a different collection entirely». `targets.json` puts **23 people** behind it. It is the only parish in the table that has never been resolved at all. One catalogue search decides whether it is reachable or whether it joins the unreachable list honestly.

---

**Half answered, 15 September 2026, and the half that is answered changes its priority.**

**Every one of the 24 people behind Gologorica is a Šestan, and not one of them is a direct ancestor.** The parish stands entirely on a married-in line. That does not make it worthless — it makes it **the last of the twenty-one parishes to spend a day on**, not the outstanding hole the row implies.

**The catalogue question is still open and could not be answered from here.** The catalogue's own search service refuses every parameter this archive knows how to send (`q.text`, `q.placeText`, `q.anyPlace` all return 400; the UI's own call to `/service/search/catalog/v3/search` returns 400 too and the page prints *«Something Went Wrong»*). **The place search wants a place id**, not a name, and getting one needs the typeahead the interface uses.

**So the row stays open with a smaller question**: not *«is Gologorica reachable»* but *«which collection holds Istrian parish registers, and is it this one»* — and it can wait behind every row that touches the direct line.

rows.what: Twenty-five children born after a parent had died — triaged
rows.note:
`consistency.json` holds **71 contradictions** and the largest class is **child-after-parent-death, 25 of them**. Each is either a wrong date, a wrong link, or two people merged into one — and this archive has already found all three kinds. They are cheap to triage against the register readings now on disk, and every one resolved either corrects the tree or produces a `corrections` row.

---

**Triaged 15 September 2026, and the triage found something the four rows did not ask about.**

**Every contradiction was supposed to be answered on the person's own page**, and `check_site.py` has a gate that says so. It read `if i.get("slug") and …` — so it **quietly excused every contradiction about a person with no page**. That is **47 of the 71 rows and 24 people**, none of them answered, and the check printed **ok** the whole time.

**It is the same blindness for the third time in one day.** Six Karlobag wives were declared outside the tree because they had no page. [Hedviga's husband's gravestone](/stones/) was filed as a stranger's because he has no page. Now the contradiction gate. **An unpublished person is invisible**, in three different tools, and each time it was found by accident.

**The gate now counts and prints them** rather than excusing them — failing only on the slugged ones, the same bargain `checkcovers` struck so a hole can be closed without the archive going red first. **[Row 55](/worklist/) carries the backlog.**

rows.what: Five duplicate groups settled without a register — and one is two boys, not one
rows.note:
`duplicates.json`: **51 groups**, of which **23 are live** and 28 already rejected. A live duplicate group is two tree records that may be one person — which is the same question as the two Georgius Urode and the seven Michaels, and it now has a settled method. **28 have already been rejected**, so the remaining 23 are the hard ones and deserve the register rather than judgement.

---

**Worked 15 September 2026. Six of the twenty-three are settled, and the tool had only half a test.**

`duplicates.py` had **`parents_conflict`** — a veto that rejects a group when two records name parents sharing no name. It had **no confirmation**: two records naming *the same* parents stayed «live» exactly like two naming nobody. So a new tier, **`same day and same parents`**, and **five groups fall into it** — same birth day, same village, same father, same mother, nothing left for a second child to be:

| Who | Born | Parents |
|---|---|---|
| Catharina Žubrinić | 20 Nov 1840, Otočac | Mate × Anna Mudrovčić |
| Josephus Žubrinić | 16 Mar 1845, Otočac | Michael × Maria Marković |
| Francisca Žubrinić | 6 Mar 1846, Otočac | Thomas × Joanna Ratković |
| Nicolaus Žubrinić | 3 Aug 1847 | Thomas × Joanna Ratković |
| Katalyn / Kate Zubrinich | 26 Jul 1886, Port Pirie | John × Rose Gormley |

**And Danijel Kalanj, 2 November 1829, Klenovica** is the plainest of all without qualifying: one copy carries his parents, the other his wife and child, and **both carry the same death date, 26 June 1876**. One man, entered twice, split down the middle.

**The sixth is not a duplicate at all, and finding that out is the point.** «*Alexander Žubrinić, 14 March 1839, Otočac*» has the same day and the same village and a **Michael** for a father in both — and the mothers are **Magdalena Orešković** and **Magdalena Mande Draženović**. Two boys, born the same day, to two different Michaels. **It is [row 1](/worklist/)'s seven Michaels in miniature**, and the first draft of the new tier declared it a duplicate, because `parents()` folds a parent to their **given names only** and both mothers reduce to *magdalena*. `parent_surnames()` now supplies the half of the name that was being thrown away.

**And the house number cannot rescue it.** Alexander is 1839, and this archive established that the Otočac baptisms **stop writing the household into *Conditio* from about 1836 to 1845**. The one instrument that separates Michaels does not reach the years where they most need separating. **The 1834–1858 deaths do carry it** — that is [row 28](/worklist/)'s finding — so the way in is a death, not a baptism.

**Seventeen groups remain**: eight *same year and place*, eight *same year only*, one *same day*. They are the hard ones, as the row said.

---

**A second sitting, and the tool had a second blind spot — this one in its keys.**

Every group above is found by keying on a **surname and a given name**, so two records can only meet if somebody spelled them alike. **pava Boras** and **Paulina Boras** never meet: the two strings share two letters and no token, so containment fails and the three-letter-prefix rule fails with it. **They are one woman.** Born **24 December 1895**, the same parents, and both married an **Ivan Krmpotić** — one copy carrying the marriage, 1917 at Senj, and no children; the other seven children and no marriage date. That is precisely the split Danijel Kalanj shows, and it was invisible.

**So a pass was added that never looks at the name.** It starts from the family: children of one couple who share an **exact birth date**. On its own that proves nothing — **this tree holds 113 such pairs** and most of them are twins, several labelled so in the tree itself. **The discriminator is the marriage. Twins do not marry the same person; a record entered twice does.**

**And it has to be the spouse's NAME, not their record.** Matching on ids found one pair and missed the Borases, because the tree holds **two Ivan Krmpotićs** — duplicating a wife duplicates her husband along with her. On names it fires **eight times** across 15,643 people, with no twin among them. Seven are married-in South African and Welsh lines; **the Borases are the only one in the Croatian material**, which is a statement about where the tree was built carelessly, not about where this pass works.

**Two tiers were being counted and never shown.** `same day and same parents` — the five groups this row added on the first sitting — was never added to `/duplicates`, so the page's total said thirteen while its tables listed eight. Both new tiers are on the page now. **A tier the reader cannot see is worse than no tier at all.**

rows.what: The by-name sweep, re-run wide — one new pair, one false friend, one lead
rows.note:
The by-name file was built out of **Selce and its neighbours**, where the connectors are *aliter · dictus · dicti* and the scribe **underlines** the pair. Karlobag, found on 15 September, uses ***vulgò*** and does **not** underline. So the sweep that produced 17 phrases **was looking for the wrong shape in every parish except one**. Re-run it across the pages already read with the connector list widened — *vulgò · alias · rečeni · zvani* — and against the surnames the tree carries as double-barrelled, which is where a by-name hides once it has been absorbed (ahnentafel 106 «Smojver Vukić» was exactly that).

---

**Re-run 15 September 2026 across every transcription on disk** — `readings.psv`, `found.psv`, `searched.json`, all of `notes/`, the film maps and the grave surveys — with the connector list widened to *aliter · alias · dictus · dicti · dicta · vulgò · rečeni · zvani · vide · ut ibi · cognomine · nuncupatus*. **123 connector phrases in 54 files.**

**Almost all of them were already in the file**, which is the answer the row wanted: the narrow sweep had not in fact missed a parish, because the Karlobag *vulgò* pairs were caught by hand the same day they were read. **Three things came out of it.**

**One new pair.** «*Verbanovich Margarita … **vide** Urbanovich … 15 9bris*» — **Verbanović ⟷ Urbanović**, on the same KAZALO page as «*Vukich vide Smojver*». It had been recorded in the film map and in the register and **never added to the by-name list**, which is exactly the gap a sweep exists to close.

**One false friend, and it matters more than the pair.** In the Otočac ***status animarum***, «*dictus / dicti*» is **not a connector at all** — it is the Latin for *«of the aforesaid»*. «*Michael filius dictus Georgij*» is Michael **son of the said George**; «*Marcus et Josephus … Georgii dicti Gemelli*» is **the twins of the said George**, not a household called Gemelli. **A sweep that harvests every *dicti* invents by-names out of pronouns.** The test — *does the word sit between two names* — is now written at the top of `bynames.psv` so the next sweep does not have to rediscover it.

**And one lead that cannot be closed from disk.** The Karlobag marriages of **1806, folio 3**, list a groom as «*Vulgo Zalic*» — a *vulgò* with **the surname it attaches to missing from the summary table**. It needs that page reopened, not another sweep.

**Still not in the list, and correctly so:** «*Georgius Saldatich aliter Venesarich*» and «*Catharina Polich aliter Antich*», both on image 304 of the Selce deaths. They were read at **half scale** and reading is reading.

rows.what: Audit the film numbers in holdings.psv — and the answer is that the catalogue counts items, not films
rows.note:
**Done in nineteen HTTP calls, 15 September 2026, and the answer is better than the audit this row planned.** The row was going to open every film and guess. It did not need to: `/service/search/catalog/item/koha:<n>` returns one `film_note` entry **per ITEM**, each with its `digital_film_no`, its **physical roll number** and its **item range**. Nineteen calls, eighty-two films, written verbatim to **`sources/familysearch/filmnotes.psv`** and checked against a second fetch by SHA-256 before being committed.

**«A film number is not a book» is now explained, not just observed.** The catalogue's unit is the *item*; the viewer's unit is the *roll*. A roll carries several items and **the items on one roll need not come from one parish**.

> **Karlobag's baptisms 1691–1804 are DGS 5481648 — *items 4 to 5 of roll 1419107*. Items 1 to 3 of that same roll are the parish of KAPTOL**, `koha:655210`, three hundred kilometres inland. So `/search/film/005481648` opens the roll at item 1 and lands in Kaptol. That is exactly what happened here, and it cost a sitting.

**Thirty-one of the eighty-two films do not begin at item 1**, across **seventeen of the nineteen parishes**. Trsat's oldest register is *item 8*. Bribir's is *item 7*. Those are the films a DGS number cannot reach, and they must be opened by waypoint.

**The same shape explains Otočac.** DGS 5482656 is *item 6* of roll 1536689 — five items of something else come first — and 5482657 is catalogued as births *and* deaths because it is *items 1–2*, two books, which is why walking it gives 483 images of baptisms and then END OF ROLL.

**And a book can have two film numbers.** Ledenice's registers were filmed twice: roll 1419155 (DGS 5482218) and roll 2119536 (DGS 5498069) are **the same three books**, decades apart. Neither is wrong. `holdings.psv` had only the first.

**One real gap closed.** Brinje sat in `holdings.psv` as *«film notes not pulled»* with no DGS number at all — and nothing noticed, because nothing compared the file with its source. It is **DGS 5498262** (Rođeni 1888-1900, Vjenčani 1888-1899) and **5498263** (Umrli 1888-1899). That is [row 50](/worklist/) answered as a side effect. **`tools/holdingscheck.py` now gates the build** so the summary can never again claim a year the catalogue does not have.

rows.what: The walls were re-graded — one had stopped being a wall, and the tool could not see it
rows.note:
**Done, 15 September 2026, and the answer was not the one this row expected.** The walls are drawn on [our line](/tree/). `walls.json` was **byte-identical at every commit this week** — 9 unplaced, 7 nameless, 6 outside, 4 reachable — while **nine direct ancestors were read**. That looked like a correct null and was not.

**`walls.py` could not see the reading.** It loads `ancestors.json` and `placefixes.json` and nothing else: the parish table tells it what is **filmed**, and nothing told it what had been **read**. So it printed «*This wall is reachable and **has not been opened***» on four walls, and for three of them the register had been opened by this archive that same morning.

**And one wall was false.** Ahnentafel **220, Nicolaus Gerkacs**, read «*No place is recorded for this household anywhere on the line, so there is no register to open. **The wall here is a place, not a name.***» His death entry puts him **in his son Antonius's house at Karlobag**. The tree has no birthplace for him; a document does.

**Both fixed at the tool.** `walls.py` now reads `sources/readings.psv` and says which documents are held and **which book is still shut**. `sources/walls.psv` is created with a format — `ahn|field|value` — where **`place`** supplies a place read off a document and **`why`** cites it; a place does *not* assert a grade, it is fed back through the normal grading so the kind stays derived.

**And the re-grade names the next job.** Ahnentafel **104, 108, 212 and 220** all want the same book — **Karlobag baptisms, 1691–1861, filmed, and nobody has opened it for any of them.** Four walls, one sitting, and it is the highest-yield unopened book on the chart.

rows.what: The two Croatian surveys are in graves.json and on the site — 56 Find a Grave memorials still match nobody
rows.note:
**The first job is done, 15 September 2026: `sources/graves/*.psv` is wired in and published at [/stones/](/stones/).** `tools/graves.py` now reads the photographed surveys beside the Find a Grave harvest and **keeps the two kinds of evidence apart by construction** — every top-level key of `graves.json` still counts the **index** and nothing else, so [Port Pirie](/port-pirie/)'s «*72 memorials and not one of them is in Croatia*» stays true. The surveys live under `stones`.

**226 names, 137 of them `r`.** Otočac 32, Senj 194. **16 match a person here** and **66 stones carry more than one name**, which is the same household claim a plot number makes.

**Two things the wiring taught that the files alone did not.**

* **A Croatian stone gives a married woman under her husband's surname.** Matching on the maiden name alone missed ahnentafel 3, 5 and 7 outright. The matcher now tries `rel.spouses` too, and marks those matches as made through a marriage. That is three direct ancestors recovered by one rule.
* **The ±1 birth-year drift is not a Senj quirk and it does not run one way.** Putting the disagreements side by side surfaced a third — **Franjo Žubrinić at Otočac, 1846 on the stone for 1845 in the tree** — and showed that an earlier note's claim that the stones were *consistently* a year early was **wrong**. Ljubomir's is early; the other two are late. Corrected in the note, the register and the page. **Three disagreements, all births, all one year, against not one death year in dispute in 226 names.**

**The matcher reuses the archive's own vocabulary** — `givennames.json` already knew that Stjepan is Stephannes and that **Franjo is not Franciska**, which is what stopped the first draft joining a man to a woman. Only an **`r`** row may contradict the tree: a `p` digit is not evidence and has been wrong four times.

**What is left is the original second job.** **56 of the 72 Find a Grave memorials still match nobody**, and **210 of the 226 stone names** likewise. Some are collateral lines, some are the *found* people of [row 47](/worklist/), some are strangers. The house numbers from row 1 give a handle at Otočac; at Senj the surnames are this family's — Prpić, Špalj, Papić, Vukelić, Tomljanović, Boras.

---

**The matcher was reading the register file, not the tree — and it was the fifth tool in this archive caught doing it.**

`graves.py` matched stones against **`people.json` and nothing else**. That is not the tree, and it is not even everyone with a page: **fifty-two direct ancestors sit in `ancestors.json` and not in it**, so their graves could not match by construction. Beyond both is everyone who exists only as a name on somebody else's record — a parent, a spouse, a child — **with no page and no slug**.

**Sixteen matches became twenty-one, and every new one is a person with no page.** Martin, Lucija and Kata Špalj; Nikola Šojat; and **Ivan Defrančeski, 1925–1995, Hedviga's husband** — who now matches his own gravestone **because the matcher was taught where to look**, not because somebody wrote a correction by hand. That is the difference between fixing an instance and fixing a tool, and this archive had been doing the first.

**One person turned out to be claimed by two stones.** Two Senj stones read **KATA ŠPALJ** — *1884–1975* and *1886–1981* — and the tree holds exactly **one** Kate Špalj, born 1886, with **no death recorded**. Both matched her, because a match needs a year within two and there was no death year to disagree with. **The better-scoring stone keeps the match, the other is unmatched again, a tie drops both, and the contest is published either way.** One of those two women is not in this tree, and publishing her under somebody else's name would be the Defrančeski mistake run backwards: **not a person missed, a person invented.**

**What is left is what was always left**: 56 Find a Grave memorials and 205 stone names matching nobody. The pool they are matched against is now the right pool, which is the precondition for the rest.

rows.what: Four of the found people were in the tree — and one of them is Hedviga's husband
rows.note:
**Done, 15 September 2026, and it caught the thing it was written to catch.** The row said each of the found people needed re-testing **against parent and spouse references, not just published names**, because this archive had already been wrong that way once. It was wrong that way again, and worse.

**Four rows came out of `found.psv`.**

* **Thomas Žubrinić, 1846** — published, and both parents match: Michael Žubrinić × Helena Orešković.
* **Luce Žubrinić, 1850** — published, both parents match: Mio × Jele Orešković.
* **Helena Orešković** — in the tree as a **parent reference with no page of her own**, which is precisely the Karlobag-wives case repeating.
* **IVAN DEFRANČESKI, 1925–1995** — recorded from [the Senj gravestone](/stones/) as *«the surname does not occur once in this archive's tree»*. **He is Hedviga's husband.** The tree carries *Ivan Anton Defrančeski, b. 1925 d. 1995*, on her own marriage, with a **null slug** because he is not published — so a search of `people.json` returns nothing. Both dates match the stone exactly. **The archive photographed the grave of the man at its centre and filed him as a stranger for a day.**

**The lesson was already written down and did not stop it happening**, so it is a gate now. **`tools/foundcheck.py`** tests every `found.psv` row against **every name in the tree** — published people and every `rel.parents`, `rel.spouses`, `rel.siblings` and `rel.children` reference — two ways: *name + year within one*, and *name + BOTH parents agreeing*. A match a person has looked at and dismissed goes in a `SETTLED` table **with the reason**; anything else **fails the build**. It runs as `check:found`.

**Eighteen people remain in `found.psv`** — the number this row started with, arrived at honestly. Three still resemble somebody in the tree and all three are settled in writing: *Maria Rosaria Antić* (ahnentafel 24 has no children published at all), *Maria Magdalena Theresia* and *Maria Žubrinić* (the parents fail the test), and **Matilda Papić, who probably IS Franka or Sulka** — the open question [row 53](/worklist/) left standing, not an error.
